+title: 'Web: add live fetch, guard, and runCode tests to WebIntegrationTests'
+---
+## What
+Add the live suites that fetch real pages and run the goal snippet, with no model. Design: `web.md` § "Testing / Level 2", rows `FetchLiveTests`, `GuardLiveTests`, `WebRunCodeLiveTests`.
+
+Create under `WebIntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolWebIntegrationTests/`, each `.serialized` with `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))`:
+- `FetchLiveTests.swift`: `https://example.com` (title `Example Domain`, content contains `Example Domain`); `http://github.com` (final URL starts with `https://github.com`); `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swift_(programming_language)` with `maxCharacters: 2000` (a `nextOffset`, and a second window of the same `WebCapability` gives the next text with no second download); `https://api.github.com/zen` (`contentType` `text/plain`, content not empty); `https://www.w3.org/WAI/ER/tests/xhtml/testfiles/resources/pdf/dummy.pdf` (the binary correction).
+- `GuardLiveTests.swift`: `http://localtest.me/` (a public DNS name that resolves to `127.0.0.1`): the correction names the loopback address; `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`: a correction.
+- `WebRunCodeLiveTests.swift`: a real `MultiTool` with `.withWeb(configuration: .keyless)` runs the snippet of `web.md` § "Goal" and returns 1 to 3 pages, each with a title and content.
+
+To prove "no second download", read through one capability instance and count requests with a `URLProtocol` that records and forwards to the network, or assert on timing no stricter than "the second call is served from the cache" by the cache hit counter that `WebPageReader` exposes for tests.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Each case above passes on a machine with network access.
+- [ ] No test retries.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] The three files above.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --package-path WebIntegrationTests --no-parallel`. All pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #web
\ No newline at end of file

+    - `Fetch(context:).call(arguments:)` gives the fetch result. `WebContext(configuration:sessionConfiguration:)` uses the real `SystemHostResolver`, thus the guard tests go through real DNS.
+    - `WebPageReader.networkLoadCount` is actor state: read it with `await context.reader.networkLoadCount`.
+    - Exact guard texts (from `WebAddressGuard`): `The address is not allowed: localtest.me resolves to 127.0.0.1, a loopback address.` and `The address is not allowed: the host 169.254.169.254 is on the blocklist.` The second is a blocklist refusal before DNS, thus it sends no request.
+    - Exact binary text (from `WebFetcher`): `The content type is not text: application/pdf. fetch reads text, HTML, JSON, and XML.`
+    - `FetchResult.contentType` holds the media type with no parameters, thus `text/plain` compares exactly.
+    - The unit fixtures `RunOutput` and `WebRun` are in the root test target. The `WebIntegrationTests` package cannot import them.
+    - DuckDuckGo challenge decision: `.keyless` tries `braveHTML` first. A DuckDuckGo challenge can reach the runCode test only after Brave fails. Then Brave's failure is the real failure. The test does not assert which keyless provider answered, and does not read `notes`. Thus a DuckDuckGo challenge alone cannot fail it.
